correctness.rationale: All diamonds require the universal apex as their degree-three vertex, so their rim triples are paths of length two or triangles. The apex gives n distinct spoke colors, an edge needs at least three in its local triangle, an apex-plus-P3 diamond forces five, and C3 or C4 requires six (for C4 two fresh rim colors beyond four spoke colors). A matching construction arranges spoke colors consecutively along every path/cycle component; on paths use j+3 modulo the palette (or a third color for isolated edges), on long cycles use vertex j+3, and on C3/C4 use separate three/two outside colors. All diamonds are intra-component, hence no cross-component conflicts; exceptions n=1..5 are covered. An independent conflict graph generator and exact coloring solver tested all 305 labeled maximum-degree-two graphs on <=5 vertices; the finite checks supplement this unrestricted proof.
